study.question: On the under_normalized host with the norm seed and lifecycle v2, does the graft's germination timing (graft_epoch 0-5) or the training horizon (10 vs 20 epochs) change how much of static capacity's gain the graft captures?
study.stop_condition_owner_signed: PDR-0054: if neither timing nor horizon changes the outcome (capture stays flat and static still wins), the ladder stops at rung 4; location or a different host proceeds only through a new owner decision.
based_on: graft-capture-v2-norm (rung 3): graft at epoch 2 captures 0.60 [0.51, 0.72] of static's gain; graft - static +0.057 [+0.028, +0.086]; the gap narrowed toward the horizon (descriptive). Seen.

Three pilots read for spread and stability (sds, divergence counts, replay checks). Pilots 1-2 (seeds 9301-9324, 144 runs) predate the prefix-stable future; pilot 3 (seeds 9330-9353, 144 runs) is on the launch runner and sizes the study: timing T0 - T3 sd 0.079 (95% UCL 0.105); horizon (gap20 - gap10) sd 0.173 (UCL 0.230); per-cell graft - static sd 0.146-0.198. Graft divergences 2/288 pilot runs across all three (T0 1, T3 1, both in pilot 3); H20 replayed T2 bitwise over its first ten epochs on all 24 pilot-3 seeds.

units.definition: one training seed; every cell of a seed shares initialisation and the minibatch order prefix, and runs on one GPU
units.population_note: Inference covers training randomness on one fixed data sample (data_seed 20261004), the under_normalized host and the norm seed.

endpoint.metric: development cross-entropy (nats) over all 5,000 dev examples, mean over the last 3 epochs of each cell's horizon (7-9 at 10 epochs, 17-19 at 20)

reading_probabilities.method: 200 simulated 768-seed studies per row through the committed timing_study.evaluate, using docs/prereg/rung4-timing-horizon-sizing.py.txt (seed effect shared across the 10-epoch cells; H20 continues T2 plus independent noise). Spreads from pilot 3 at its point estimate and its 95% UCL.

predictions.expected_reading: No direction is predicted: the pilots were not read for means. lever_found if timing or horizon moves capture favourably beyond its margin; flat_stop if both are flat everywhere and static still wins.
predictions.would_surprise: graft_unstable, instrument_failure (including a prefix-replay mismatch between H20 and T2), or changes_adversely on timing (later grafting better).

disclosures: Rung 3 numbers were seen. The pilots' analysis reports also contain cell means and contrasts; the author extracted only sds, divergence counts and replay checks from them, and no design choice was changed after seeing them.

Margins: delta_timing 0.02 nats is about 14% of static's 0.144-nat gain over no growth on this host (rung 3), so 'timing flat' means every 10-epoch cell's graft late CE lies within about 14 capture points of T2's; delta_horizon 0.05 nats (about 35 points) reflects the noisier 20-epoch arm. A 0.03 timing effect or a mid-range peak never reads flat_stop in simulation (statistics review).

n = 768 is chosen so a truly flat world reaches flat_stop with probability 0.97 at pilot 3's 95% UCL spreads (1.0 at the point spreads). Jobs on nyx need no permission (PDR-0056); the cost is about 16 h on two GPUs.

Per-contrast handling: a seed enters a contrast if and only if both of its arms finished; divergences are counted per cell (graft) and per seed-horizon (static) with exact bounds and gate the reading; no unit is re-run.

Caps (computed): graft 24 per cell of 768 (3.1%; pilot rate 2/288 = 0.7%, exact one-sided 95% upper 2.2%). graft_unstable is the maximum over six positively correlated cells, so its study-level probability is at most 0.08 at a true 2% per-cell rate and about 0.94 at 3%. Static 80 of 1,536 seed-horizons (5.2%): P(exceed) is 0.008 at a true 4% rate, 0.33 at 5%. Failed runs 8 of 4,608: P(exceed) 0.045 at a 0.1% crash rate.

The runner's common future is prefix-stable (bounded_comparison.draw_future): H20 continues T2 bitwise for ten epochs, a replay test the analysis enforces. The kernel's CommonFuture is untouched; runs from earlier studies are not reproducible at this runner (their source identity already differs).
Timing contrast T0 - T3: T5's late window lies in blending, so T5 enters only the flatness requirement and the descriptive slope.

Execution profile: GPU, Academy-exact per SKU (2x RTX 4060 Ti), one process per GPU, every cell of a seed on one device, from one immutable snapshot; data identity pinned and checked before launch; an interrupted fleet resumes from its own snapshot (timing_study launch --resume).
deviations: Pre-launch amendments after three Fable reviews of 3bdf81e (statistics, product, code): per-contrast margins (timing 0.02), timing contrast T0-T3, flat_stop requires every 10-epoch cell flat against T2, beyond_floor split by sign (changes_adversely), prefix-stable common future and its replay test, resume, stricter plan validation, n 384 -> 768 after a re-pilot on the launch runner.
